## Rejected as needless churn (do NOT do these)

The next agent must **not** attempt the following. Each was considered and rejected
with a baseline-grounded or pressure-grounded reason; log none of them as work, only
to `V1-CANDIDATES.md` if a real need later appears.

1. **Make `deadreckon-core`'s `pub mod` declarations private and route everything
   through flat re-exports.** Consumers already deep-path into core
   (`deadreckon_core::campaign::ENV_SUB_RESULT`, `::plan::PLAN_NARRATIVE`,
   `::plan::PLAN_DOCS_DIR`, `::campaign::read_sub_result`, `::campaign::SubResult`,
   `::docs::*` in runtime), and several of those items are NOT in the flattened
   re-export list. This breaks internal callers AND rewrites ~268 baseline lines for
   zero product benefit. **Reject.**
2. **Encapsulate `Chain`/`Plan`/`PlanTask`/`ChainStep` fields behind semantic
   transition methods** (`mark_step_running`, etc.). ~74+ call sites in the monolith, a
   public-surface change on the most-used core types, high break risk for
   forward-flexibility the product does not need. The audit rates it risk:high/large.
   **Reject as churn.**
3. **Add `#[non_exhaustive]` / accessors to `SpendEstimate`, `ProviderRouteInfo`, or
   wrap `PlanTask.depends_on` in a newtype.** Speculative API-evolution insurance with
   no concrete pressure and a baseline impact. **Reject until a real evolution need
   appears.**
4. **Split `cli.rs`'s 45-variant `Command` enum and inline help consts into per-family
   files with re-exports.** A rename/relocation diff that keeps the enum identical to
   callers; the dispatcher refactor (P4–P5) delivers the navigability win without
   churning the parse layer. **Reject.**
5. **Introduce a uniform `CommandHandler` trait / `cli()->exec()` shape across all
   handlers.** Cosmetic standardization with one caller each; the thin dispatch match
   already unblocks middleware. **Reject.**
6. **Move binary CLI logic into a fat `lib.rs` with `pub run(cli) -> ExitCode` for
   external reuse.** No second frontend or external consumer exists; this adds a public
   surface and maintenance contract for hypothetical reuse. **Defer/reject until a real
   library consumer exists.**
7. **Add `#[source]` to `ProviderError::Http`/`Cli` and adopt sysexits granular exit
   codes.** Behavior-adjacent (changes error chains / exit signals) with no current
   consumer inspecting them; out of scope for an equivalence-preserving refactor.
   **Reject.**
8. **Reorganize large integration test files (`orchestrate.rs`, 176 tests) into feature
   submodules and add per-test doc comments.** Pure cosmetic reshuffling neither clippy
   nor rustfmt requested, inflating diffs reviewers must re-verify. **Reject.**

Child work stays normal `deadreckon` subprocesses (§30.1). Depth **hard-capped at 2** — sub-orchestrators cannot fan out again. No `git push`. Edits inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Depth>2, cross-level dependencies/merge-repair, recursive live attach → `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
12	
13	**User contract.**
14	
15	- `deadreckon campaign <goal> --n <2..=6>` previews mode, N, depth cap, tree budget, and provider roles, then (with `--yes`) launches N independent sub-orchestrators and composes their results.
16	- A campaign invoked from inside a sub-orchestrator (depth would reach 2) is **refused**; no meta-plan is written. A sub-goal resolving to an ancestor's `task_key`/scope is **refused** (cycle guard).
17	- `--max-spend` is a **tree ceiling**: split across sub-orchestrators, aggregate spend tracked across every leaf run; the meta refuses to launch more once exhausted.
18	- The campaign result reports **clean only if every leaf run signed clean**; any refused leaf fails the campaign, any caveat leaf surfaces a caveat (roll-up over §35 verdicts).
19	- `attach <campaign-id>` shows the N sub-plan rows with a breadcrumb; `kill <campaign-id>` cascades to sub-coordinators and their children; `show <campaign-id> --why-failed` explains a failed campaign.
20	
21	**Phases.** Eleven (P1-P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first -> implement -> focused tests green -> conventional local commit -> CHANGELOG. P1 lands the depth/cycle/lineage guard (RED first). P11 adds AS-BUILT §36 and logs deferrals.

24	
25	- Every rider depth test present and passing; `cargo fmt --check`; `git diff --check`.
26	- Smoke (smoke provider, `--sandbox none`): a 2-sub-goal campaign launches two sub-orchestrators, composes one promoted result, and `campaign-rollup.json` records both leaf verdicts.
27	- Smoke: a campaign attempted at depth 2 is **refused** (no meta-plan, clear reason).
28	- Smoke: one leaf refused (hollow pass) makes the **campaign fail**, never `Completed`; one leaf caveat surfaces a caveat on the meta summary.
29	- No edits outside the repo; no `git push`; no `Plan`/`PlanTask`/`PipelineState` schema changes.
30	
31	**Stop when** verification passes, campaign launches N orchestrators within the depth cap and tree budget, the meta-merge produces one promoted run, the gate roll-up refuses on any leaf refusal, attach/kill/why-failed work for campaigns, AS-BUILT and CHANGELOG record the behavior, deferrals are in V1-CANDIDATES, and the work is committed locally.

GOAL: Decompose the 40k-line binary `main.rs` behind a stable facade. Today the `deadreckon` binary crate is one 40,597-line `main.rs`: ~11k lines of flat command handlers and helpers plus ~29k lines of inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules, a single global namespace with no `commands/` structure, so every change forces a triple-edit and reviewers cannot navigate it. Because the binary crate is **not** part of the public-surface baseline (only the four library crates are), relocating it into private domain modules is genuinely zero-public-surface-risk — but only once a CLI-output characterization net exists, since the current integration tests assert state and files, not stdout/stderr formatting. This lands that net first, lifts the inline test modules out, then carves command families (chain/orchestrate/plan/campaign/attach) and the TUI render layer into private `commands/` and `tui/` modules behind a thin `main_inner` dispatcher, re-exporting nothing new. A tight set of cheap library cleanups follows. Headline word: **Decompose**.

**Read first.**

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` — substrate; latest section is §37.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/DATESLUG-rider.md` — full contract, eleven phases.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` (40,597 lines) and `.../src/cli.rs` — the targets.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/tests/.public-surface-baseline` — the surface that must not move.
- Prior riders in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — invariants hold.

**Posture.** Behavior-preserving refactor only: every command's stdout/stderr, exit codes, and file/state side effects stay byte-identical. `make verify` (fmt --check + clippy -D warnings + public-surface + `cargo test --workspace` + release build) is green at **every** commit, including each module-move commit. The public-surface baseline is unchanged; the binary crate is not in it, so binary decomposition cannot touch it. No schema or behavior changes. Module moves are mechanical: relocate code, widen visibility only to `pub(crate)` (never `pub`), never edit logic in the same commit as a move. No `git push`. Edits inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Needless-churn items are rejected; major decisions and deferrals → `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.

**Workstreams** (in order). (1) Lay a CLI-output characterization net — golden snapshots of stdout/stderr for plan/orchestrate/chain/attach and error footers — *before* anything moves. (2) Lift the seven inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules out of `main.rs` to `tests/`, shrinking the source ~70%. (3) Carve command families into `src/commands/{chain/,orchestrate.rs,plan.rs,campaign.rs,attach.rs,run.rs,init.rs,acceptance.rs,merge.rs}` behind a thin `main_inner` match. (4) Extract the pure TUI render layer into `src/tui/`. (5–7) Cheap library cleanups: unify the three `compose_*` merge loops and the two command-exists impls, dedupe `is_retryable_io_kind`, prune unused `tracing`/`chrono`, delete confirmed dead code, harden the docs.rs regex init, apply measured allocation nits. **Non-goals (rejected churn):** tightening core/providers `pub mod`→`mod`; encapsulating Chain/Plan fields behind transition methods; `#[non_exhaustive]`/accessor insurance; splitting the `cli.rs` Commands enum; a uniform CommandHandler trait; a fat `pub run()` lib facade; `#[source]`/sysexits error changes; reshuffling large test files.

**Phases.** Eleven (P1–P11) in the rider, depth/characterization-tests-first (RED before refactor): P1 net, P2 shared test helpers, P3 lift inline test modules, P4 commands/ skeleton + chain family, P5 remaining families, P6 tui/, P7 merge helper, P8 command-exists, P9 `is_retryable_io_kind` (the single justified re-baseline, isolated at the tip), P10 deps/dead-code/regex/alloc nits, P11 adds **AS-BUILT §38** and logs deferrals.

**Verification.**

- `make verify` green at every commit; all workspace lints satisfied.
- Characterization snapshots captured in P1 pass **before and after** each split with zero diff.
- Public-surface baseline unchanged, except the one P9 path re-baselined with written justification in the commit.
- `cargo test --workspace` reports the same test count and names after each move.
- Concrete smoke proving equivalence: a sampled CLI command (e.g. `plan --draft`, `orchestrate preview`) produces identical stdout/stderr pre/post; an off-TTY attach render frame matches its golden.

**Stop when** verification passes, `main.rs` is decomposed behind a stable `main_inner`/`commands/`/`tui/` facade with the source file well under threshold, the characterization net is in place, AS-BUILT §38 and CHANGELOG record the new layout, deferrals are in V1-CANDIDATES, and the work is committed locally.

The workflow ran 15 agents (~887k tokens, ~22 min): 3 researched Rust best practices → 8 audited the crates across dimensions → synthesis ranked by gain/(risk+effort) → an adversarial critic cut needless churn → authored the docs.

**Files written & verified:**
- `docs/goals/2026-05-29-1600-deadreckon-decompose-goal.md` — **3993 bytes** (≤4000 cap ✓)
- `docs/goals/2026-05-29-1600-deadreckon-decompose-rider.md` — 34,168 chars, eleven phases

**The headline finding:** `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` is **40,597 lines** in one file (~11k of flat command handlers + ~29k of inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules, no `commands/` structure). Every change is a triple-edit; reviewers can't navigate it.

**The key insight that makes it safe** (factually verified): the binary crate is *not* in `tests/.public-surface-baseline` (only the 4 libs are), so relocating it into private `pub(crate)` modules is **zero public-surface risk** — provided a CLI-output characterization net exists first, since current tests assert state/files, not stdout/stderr.

**The plan — 7 workstreams, behavior-preserving, `make verify` green every commit:**
1. CLI-output characterization net (safety harness) — *first*
2. Lift inline test modules out of `main.rs`
3. Carve command families → private `commands/{chain,orchestrate,plan,campaign,…}`
4. Extract TUI render layer → private `tui/`
5. Consolidate duplicated merge + command-exists logic
6. Library cleanups (dedupe `is_retryable_io_kind`, prune deps, dead code, regex)
7. Targeted allocation nits

**What it deliberately rejects as needless churn** (so the next agent doesn't do it): core/providers `pub mod`→`mod`, encapsulating Chain/Plan fields, `#[non_exhaustive]`/accessor insurance, splitting the `cli.rs` Commands enum, a `CommandHandler` trait, a fat `pub run()` facade, `#[source]`/sysexits changes, and reshuffling test files.
